note:
ISO 2026-W03 runs from January 12 through January 18. Venus and Mars are separated by about 1.9° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 2.8° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌑 New Moon — 19:51:59 UTC. The dark Moon favors faint targets and extended star fields. Use α Dor, Aldebaran as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -9.5; direct motion; 37.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 19:51 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 15:47 UTC. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 15:11 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -0.9; direct motion; 98.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 15:47 UTC. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 07:40 UTC. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.1; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 15:11 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Jan 18 07:40 UTC. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 97.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: In solar glare; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace Caelum’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Cae at its charted position. Trace Caelum’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Cae at its charted position. Trace Camelopardalis’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Cam at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for telescope observing this week.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

No deep-sky objects are featured this week.

story_candidates.dek: α Dor is a stellar reference in Dor used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected α Dor for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Dor constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
